correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md §§1–5. For z0 z1 nonzero the ambient gradient forces t^3=4 and t^6=1; the zero-coordinate cases are nonsingular. A fiber critical point has w≠0; on w=1 its squared coordinates are (-1/3,-t/3,-t²/3,0). Neither endpoint is bad. Writing x2=δ t x0 gives the two coprime squarefree sextics and exactly two solutions at each root. The Hessian is nondegenerate in the three nonzero coordinates and x3 enters only cubically, giving A2. For the plane section the binary cubic has one double root and not a triple root (b²−3ac=9t^5 at every bad t); the binary leading coefficient cannot vanish there, and the x3³ term gives the cusp. The parameter derivative is nonzero at each critical point, so the local cubic discriminant has order two at each point. Independently, in the homogeneous gradient resultant, the x3² derivative gives the square of the resultant on x3=0, and the factor w in the w-derivative contributes only a nonzero constant. The other factor is the linear form L=x0+t x1+t² x2; evaluating it on the eight solutions of the three diagonal quadratics on w=1 gives, up to constant, D_+²D_-²: pairing the ±sqrt(t) choices gives (1±t³)²−t³. Squaring gives D^4, and the projective endpoints are smooth. Both sextics reduce to the irreducible Phi_9 modulo 2. A plus-field contains sqrt(−3) from a primitive cube root; a minus-field has a real embedding, so the quadratic point extension is nontrivial. This gives exactly the point orbits 6,6,12. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py, including the extent of the symbolic assertions; did not run the frozen script.
